evidence: The trip starts from Arthur's Pass village on SH73, 150 km from Christchurch. It finishes at Klondyke Corner 8 km south of Arthur’s Pass village.
Two tracks head to Avalanche Peak: Avalanche Peak Track is steeper and more direct; Scotts Track climbs more gradually, has better views, and is easier on the knees.
The route leaves the ridge and a scree slope takes you all the way to the Crow River.
From here you can see Crow Hut on the true right bank of Crow River.
Cross Crow River where it opens out before joining the Waimakariri River.
A gravel road takes you the final short distance to Klondyke Corner.

doubts: The page describes one route from Arthur's Pass village to Klondyke Corner, so kind and shape are one_way; the text says the trip finishes at Klondyke Corner and gives no return. DOC's time is '2 days'; the leg times (3–4 hours, 1 hour, 1 hour 30 minutes, 4 hours) are not summed. Start ref T4 is the place 'Arthur's Pass' near the village; this is inferred, not certain, and no road end matches it. The end ref T11 is the Klondyke Corner place. Two tracks go to Avalanche Peak (Avalanche Peak Track and Scotts Track) and the text does not say which is the main way, so neither is a via and both are in not_on_route. The 'See Avalanche Peak Route' link is treated as another walk, not as this way's leg. Crossings: 'Cross Crow River' and the Waimakariri crossings are marked as fords because the text gives no bridge, but whether they are fordable without a bridge is not fully stated. The Waimakariri ford has no name entry, so its ref is null. Alternatives in the text (crossing further downstream where Crow River joins the Waimakariri; the Turkey Flat traverse and track to the Bealey road bridge on SH73) are not recorded as separate ways because they have no heading or time of their own. The shuttle bus and car at Klondyke Corner are not recorded as exits.
